scene.label: Act 5, Scene 3
scene.title: SCENE III. Troy. Before Priam's palace.

lines.text: When was my lord so much ungently temper'd
lines.plainText: When was my lord so much ungently temper'd

lines.text: To stop his ears against admonishment?
lines.plainText: To stop his ears against admonishment

lines.text: Unarm, unarm, and do not fight today.
lines.plainText: Unarm unarm and do not fight today

lines.text: You train me to offend you; get you in.
lines.plainText: You train me to offend you get you in

lines.text: By all the everlasting gods, I'll go.
lines.plainText: By all the everlasting gods I'll go

lines.text: My dreams will, sure, prove ominous to the day.
lines.plainText: My dreams will sure prove ominous to the day

lines.text: No more, I say.
lines.plainText: No more I say

lines.text: Where is my brother Hector?
lines.plainText: Where is my brother Hector

lines.text: Here, sister, arm'd, and bloody in intent.
lines.plainText: Here sister arm'd and bloody in intent

lines.text: Consort with me in loud and dear petition,
lines.plainText: Consort with me in loud and dear petition

lines.text: Pursue we him on knees; for I have dreamt
lines.plainText: Pursue we him on knees for I have dreamt

lines.text: Of bloody turbulence, and this whole night
lines.plainText: Of bloody turbulence and this whole night

lines.text: Hath nothing been but shapes and forms of slaughter.
lines.plainText: Hath nothing been but shapes and forms of slaughter

lines.text: O, 'tis true!
lines.plainText: O 'tis true

lines.text: Ho! bid my trumpet sound.
lines.plainText: Ho bid my trumpet sound

lines.text: No notes of sally, for the heavens, sweet brother!
lines.plainText: No notes of sally for the heavens sweet brother

lines.text: Be gone, I say. The gods have heard me swear.
lines.plainText: Be gone I say The gods have heard me swear

lines.text: The gods are deaf to hot and peevish vows;
lines.plainText: The gods are deaf to hot and peevish vows

lines.text: They are polluted off'rings, more abhorr'd
lines.plainText: They are polluted off'rings more abhorr'd

lines.text: Than spotted livers in the sacrifice.
lines.plainText: Than spotted livers in the sacrifice

lines.text: O, be persuaded! Do not count it holy
lines.plainText: O be persuaded Do not count it holy

lines.text: To hurt by being just. It is as lawful,
lines.plainText: To hurt by being just It is as lawful

lines.text: For we would give much, to use violent thefts
lines.plainText: For we would give much to use violent thefts

lines.text: And rob in the behalf of charity.
lines.plainText: And rob in the behalf of charity

lines.text: It is the purpose that makes strong the vow;
lines.plainText: It is the purpose that makes strong the vow

lines.text: But vows to every purpose must not hold.
lines.plainText: But vows to every purpose must not hold

lines.text: Unarm, sweet Hector.
lines.plainText: Unarm sweet Hector

lines.text: Hold you still, I say.
lines.plainText: Hold you still I say

lines.text: Mine honour keeps the weather of my fate.
lines.plainText: Mine honour keeps the weather of my fate

lines.text: Life every man holds dear; but the dear man
lines.plainText: Life every man holds dear but the dear man

lines.text: Holds honour far more precious dear than life.
lines.plainText: Holds honour far more precious dear than life

lines.text: Cassandra, call my father to persuade.
lines.plainText: Cassandra call my father to persuade

lines.text: No, faith, young Troilus; doff thy harness, youth;
lines.plainText: No faith young Troilus doff thy harness youth

lines.text: I am today i' th'vein of chivalry.
lines.plainText: I am today i' th'vein of chivalry

lines.text: Let grow thy sinews till their knots be strong,
lines.plainText: Let grow thy sinews till their knots be strong

lines.text: And tempt not yet the brushes of the war.
lines.plainText: And tempt not yet the brushes of the war

lines.text: Unarm thee, go; and doubt thou not, brave boy,
lines.plainText: Unarm thee go and doubt thou not brave boy

lines.text: I'll stand today for thee and me and Troy.
lines.plainText: I'll stand today for thee and me and Troy

lines.text: Brother, you have a vice of mercy in you,
lines.plainText: Brother you have a vice of mercy in you

lines.text: Which better fits a lion than a man.
lines.plainText: Which better fits a lion than a man

lines.text: What vice is that? Good Troilus, chide me for it.
lines.plainText: What vice is that Good Troilus chide me for it

lines.text: When many times the captive Grecian falls,
lines.plainText: When many times the captive Grecian falls

lines.text: Even in the fan and wind of your fair sword,
lines.plainText: Even in the fan and wind of your fair sword

lines.text: You bid them rise and live.
lines.plainText: You bid them rise and live

lines.text: O, 'tis fair play!
lines.plainText: O 'tis fair play

lines.text: Fool's play, by heaven, Hector.
lines.plainText: Fool's play by heaven Hector

lines.text: How now? how now?
lines.plainText: How now how now

lines.text: For th' love of all the gods,
lines.plainText: For th' love of all the gods

lines.text: Let's leave the hermit Pity with our mother;
lines.plainText: Let's leave the hermit Pity with our mother

lines.text: And when we have our armours buckled on,
lines.plainText: And when we have our armours buckled on

lines.text: The venom'd vengeance ride upon our swords,
lines.plainText: The venom'd vengeance ride upon our swords

lines.text: Spur them to ruthful work, rein them from ruth!
lines.plainText: Spur them to ruthful work rein them from ruth

lines.text: Fie, savage, fie!
lines.plainText: Fie savage fie

lines.text: Hector, then 'tis wars.
lines.plainText: Hector then 'tis wars

lines.text: Troilus, I would not have you fight today.
lines.plainText: Troilus I would not have you fight today

lines.text: Who should withhold me?
lines.plainText: Who should withhold me

lines.text: Not fate, obedience, nor the hand of Mars
lines.plainText: Not fate obedience nor the hand of Mars

lines.text: Beckoning with fiery truncheon my retire;
lines.plainText: Beckoning with fiery truncheon my retire

lines.text: Not Priamus and Hecuba on knees,
lines.plainText: Not Priamus and Hecuba on knees

lines.text: Their eyes o'er-galled with recourse of tears;
lines.plainText: Their eyes o'ergalled with recourse of tears

lines.text: Nor you, my brother, with your true sword drawn,
lines.plainText: Nor you my brother with your true sword drawn

lines.text: Oppos'd to hinder me, should stop my way,
lines.plainText: Oppos'd to hinder me should stop my way

lines.text: But by my ruin.
lines.plainText: But by my ruin

lines.text: Lay hold upon him, Priam, hold him fast;
lines.plainText: Lay hold upon him Priam hold him fast

lines.text: He is thy crutch; now if thou lose thy stay,
lines.plainText: He is thy crutch now if thou lose thy stay

lines.text: Thou on him leaning, and all Troy on thee,
lines.plainText: Thou on him leaning and all Troy on thee

lines.text: Fall all together.
lines.plainText: Fall all together

lines.text: Come, Hector, come, go back.
lines.plainText: Come Hector come go back

lines.text: Thy wife hath dreamt; thy mother hath had visions;
lines.plainText: Thy wife hath dreamt thy mother hath had visions

lines.text: Cassandra doth foresee; and I myself
lines.plainText: Cassandra doth foresee and I myself

lines.text: Am like a prophet suddenly enrapt
lines.plainText: Am like a prophet suddenly enrapt

lines.text: To tell thee that this day is ominous.
lines.plainText: To tell thee that this day is ominous

lines.text: Therefore, come back.
lines.plainText: Therefore come back

lines.text: Aeneas is a-field;
lines.plainText: Aeneas is afield

lines.text: And I do stand engag'd to many Greeks,
lines.plainText: And I do stand engag'd to many Greeks

lines.text: Even in the faith of valour, to appear
lines.plainText: Even in the faith of valour to appear

lines.text: This morning to them.
lines.plainText: This morning to them

lines.text: Ay, but thou shalt not go.
lines.plainText: Ay but thou shalt not go

lines.text: I must not break my faith.
lines.plainText: I must not break my faith

lines.text: You know me dutiful; therefore, dear sir,
lines.plainText: You know me dutiful therefore dear sir

lines.text: Let me not shame respect; but give me leave
lines.plainText: Let me not shame respect but give me leave

lines.text: To take that course by your consent and voice
lines.plainText: To take that course by your consent and voice

lines.text: Which you do here forbid me, royal Priam.
lines.plainText: Which you do here forbid me royal Priam

lines.text: O Priam, yield not to him!
lines.plainText: O Priam yield not to him

lines.text: Do not, dear father.
lines.plainText: Do not dear father

lines.text: Andromache, I am offended with you.
lines.plainText: Andromache I am offended with you

lines.text: Upon the love you bear me, get you in.
lines.plainText: Upon the love you bear me get you in

lines.text: This foolish, dreaming, superstitious girl
lines.plainText: This foolish dreaming superstitious girl

lines.text: Makes all these bodements.
lines.plainText: Makes all these bodements

lines.text: O, farewell, dear Hector!
lines.plainText: O farewell dear Hector

lines.text: Look how thou diest. Look how thy eye turns pale.
lines.plainText: Look how thou diest Look how thy eye turns pale

lines.text: Look how thy wounds do bleed at many vents.
lines.plainText: Look how thy wounds do bleed at many vents

lines.text: Hark how Troy roars; how Hecuba cries out;
lines.plainText: Hark how Troy roars how Hecuba cries out

lines.text: How poor Andromache shrills her dolours forth;
lines.plainText: How poor Andromache shrills her dolours forth

lines.text: Behold distraction, frenzy, and amazement,
lines.plainText: Behold distraction frenzy and amazement

lines.text: Like witless antics, one another meet,
lines.plainText: Like witless antics one another meet

lines.text: And all cry, 'Hector! Hector's dead! O Hector!'
lines.plainText: And all cry 'Hector Hector's dead O Hector'

lines.text: Away, away!
lines.plainText: Away away

lines.text: Farewell! yet, soft! Hector, I take my leave.
lines.plainText: Farewell yet soft Hector I take my leave

lines.text: Thou dost thyself and all our Troy deceive.
lines.plainText: Thou dost thyself and all our Troy deceive

lines.text: You are amaz'd, my liege, at her exclaim.
lines.plainText: You are amaz'd my liege at her exclaim

lines.text: Go in, and cheer the town; we'll forth, and fight,
lines.plainText: Go in and cheer the town we'll forth and fight

lines.text: Do deeds worth praise and tell you them at night.
lines.plainText: Do deeds worth praise and tell you them at night

lines.text: Farewell. The gods with safety stand about thee!
lines.plainText: Farewell The gods with safety stand about thee

lines.text: They are at it, hark! Proud Diomed, believe,
lines.plainText: They are at it hark Proud Diomed believe

lines.text: I come to lose my arm or win my sleeve.
lines.plainText: I come to lose my arm or win my sleeve

lines.text: Do you hear, my lord? Do you hear?
lines.plainText: Do you hear my lord Do you hear

lines.text: What now?
lines.plainText: What now

lines.text: Here's a letter come from yond poor girl.
lines.plainText: Here's a letter come from yond poor girl

lines.text: Let me read.
lines.plainText: Let me read

lines.text: A whoreson tisick, a whoreson rascally tisick, so troubles me, and the foolish fortune of this girl, and what one thing, what another, that I shall leave you one o' these days; and I have a rheum in mine eyes too, and such an ache in my bones that unless a man were curs'd I cannot tell what to think on't. What says she there?
lines.plainText: A whoreson tisick a whoreson rascally tisick so troubles me and the foolish fortune of this girl and what one thing what another that I shall leave you one o' these days and I have a rheum in mine eyes too and such an ache in my bones that unless a man were curs'd I cannot tell what to think on't What says she there

lines.text: Words, words, mere words, no matter from the heart;
lines.plainText: Words words mere words no matter from the heart

lines.text: Th'effect doth operate another way.
lines.plainText: Th'effect doth operate another way
